title: Descending cycles in a kernel-closed exact-image class
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive, meaning that it preserves addition and zero of morphisms. Let $\mathcal E$ be a class of objects of $\mathcal A$ containing every zero object and closed under isomorphisms. Assume that for every short exact sequence $0\to M'\xrightarrow{i}M\xrightarrow{p}M''\to0$ with $M,M''\in\mathcal E$, one has $M'\in\mathcal E$ and $0\to V(M')\xrightarrow{V(i)}V(M)\xrightarrow{V(p)}V(M'')\to0$ is short exact. Let $E$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $b\in\mathbf Z$, and suppose $E^n=0$ for $n>b$, $H^n(E)=0$ for every $n$, and $E^n\in\mathcal E$ for every $n$. Write $Z^n(E)=\ker d_E^n$, let $i_n:Z^n(E)\to E^n$ be its inclusion, and let $p_n:E^n\to Z^{n+1}(E)$ be the differential with codomain restricted to cycles. Then $Z^n(E)\in\mathcal E$ for every $n$, and
$$0\to V(Z^n(E))\xrightarrow{V(i_n)}V(E^n)\xrightarrow{V(p_n)}V(Z^{n+1}(E))\to0$$
is short exact for every $n$. In the termwise image complex $V(E)$, the map $V(i_n)$ identifies $V(Z^n(E))$ with both $\ker d_{V(E)}^n$ and $\operatorname{im}d_{V(E)}^{n-1}$ as subobjects of $V(E^n)$. In particular $V(E)$ is acyclic. Neither right exactness of $V$ on the whole category nor enough projectives is assumed.

proof.text: Put $a_n:E^{n-1}\to Z^n(E)$ for the cycle lift of $d_E^{n-1}$. By the cohomology definition, $H^n(E)$ is its cokernel. This cokernel is zero. For every $z:T\to Z^n(E)$, clause (c) of the refinement lemma therefore gives an epimorphism $\rho:T'\to T$ and $x:T'\to E^{n-1}$ with $z\rho=a_nx$. Clause (a) makes $a_n$ epic. Thus $p_n=a_{n+1}$ is epic. Also $d_E^n=i_{n+1}p_n$, so the monicity of $i_{n+1}$ gives $\ker p_n=\ker d_E^n$, with inclusion $i_n$. Hence $0\to Z^n(E)\xrightarrow{i_n}E^n\xrightarrow{p_n}Z^{n+1}(E)\to0$ is short exact for every $n$.

proof.text: For $n>b$, $Z^n(E)$ is zero because it is the kernel of a map from the zero object $E^n$; hence it belongs to $\mathcal E$. Starting with $Z^{b+1}(E)\in\mathcal E$, induct on $k\in\mathbf N$ to obtain $Z^{b+1-k}(E)\in\mathcal E$. At the successor step set $n=b-k$: Step 1 gives the short exact cycle sequence, $E^n\in\mathcal E$ by hypothesis and $Z^{n+1}(E)\in\mathcal E$ by induction. The assumed closure condition gives $Z^n(E)\in\mathcal E$ and the stated short exact image sequence. This also gives that image sequence for $n>b$, since its middle and quotient are in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Dual of Tag 015D, lemma-F-acyclic-ses, used in the acyclic-computation setting of Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity; explicit induction using the class condition assumed in this item.

proof.text: Write $I_n=V(i_n)$ and $P_n=V(p_n)$. Step 2 says that $I_n$ is monic, $P_n$ is epic, and $\operatorname{im}I_n=\ker P_n$. The image of the monomorphism $I_n$ is the subobject it represents. Functoriality gives $d_{V(E)}^n=I_{n+1}P_n$. As $I_{n+1}$ is monic, an arrow $x$ satisfies $d_{V(E)}^nx=0$ exactly when $P_nx=0$. Thus $\ker d_{V(E)}^n=\ker P_n=\operatorname{im}I_n$ as subobjects, with representative $I_n$.

source.place: Tag 010E, definition-exact; kernel universal property and cancellation of the monomorphism supplied by Step 2.

proof.text: The factorization $d_{V(E)}^{n-1}=I_nP_{n-1}$ gives $d_{V(E)}^nd_{V(E)}^{n-1}=0$. If $x:T\to V(E^n)$ satisfies $d_{V(E)}^nx=0$, Step 3 gives $x=I_nz$. Since $P_{n-1}$ is epic, clause (a) supplies an epimorphism $\rho:T'\to T$ and $y:T'\to V(E^{n-1})$ with $z\rho=P_{n-1}y$. Thus $x\rho=d_{V(E)}^{n-1}y$. Clause (b) proves exactness at $V(E^n)$, namely $\operatorname{im}d_{V(E)}^{n-1}=\ker d_{V(E)}^n$. Step 3 identifies this common subobject with $I_n$. Its quotient is zero in every degree, so $V(E)$ is acyclic.
